chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ibrahim, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you depart [from Mina] and reach al-Hasbah, which is al-Batha', and you wish to stay for a short while, then indeed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed my father (peace be upon him) used to stay there, then depart and enter Mecca without sleeping in it.' And he said: 'Indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) only stayed there where he sent Aisha with her brother Abd al-Rahman to al-Tan'im, so she performed 'Umrah due to the reason that had befallen her, so she circled the Ka'bah, then performed Sa'i, then returned, and he departed on that same day.'

key_terms.الْبَطْحَاء: Al-Batha', another name for the area of al-Hasbah
key_terms.الْعِلَّة: Illness or valid reason for exemption

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice for staying at al-Batha' when departing from Mina during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the Sunnah of lingering briefly at al-Hasbah (al-Batha') upon departing Mina, a practice attributed to Imam al-Baqir and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). It highlights the historical precedent of Aisha performing her 'Umrah from this specific location due to illness, thereby establishing al-Hasbah as a significant site for pilgrims to pause before entering Mecca to complete their rituals.
